headline: Trump, Xi and Putin Assigned to Same Group Project; Earth Begs to Switch Groups
subheadline: Sources confirm all three members have already claimed they are the only one doing any work.
author: Dennis Whitfield-Prague, Foreign Affairs Desk
seoTitle: Trump Xi Putin Trilateral Summit: Group Project
seoDescription: Satire: Trump arrives in China for a trilateral summit with Xi and Putin that has all the hallmarks of a middle-school group project.
sourceEvent: US President Donald Trump arrived in China, where he was greeted by Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of a trilateral summit also set to include Russian President Vladimir Putin. The meeting of the three leaders is expected to draw global attention.

altHeadlines: Xi Already Started the Poster Board; Putin Insists He'll Do the Slides
Trilateral Summit Enters 'Please Just Present and Sit Down' Phase

body:
BEIJING — US President Donald Trump arrived in China on Tuesday, where he was personally greeted by Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of a trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin — an event diplomatic sources have confirmed is functionally identical to a middle-school group project, only with nuclear weapons.

The three leaders are expected to spend the coming days seated around a table none of them chose, discussing a shared deliverable none of them have read, while each privately assures reporters he is "the only one doing any actual work on this thing."

Organisers confirmed the summit will open, as tradition demands, with a forty-minute argument about whose name goes first on the cover page.

**Everyone is carrying the group, sources confirm**

A spokesperson for the Chinese delegation said Xi had "already started the poster board" and brought the good markers, and was "frankly tired of being the only one who reads the assignment brief." A Kremlin aide, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Putin had "written most of the report already" and would "handle the slides," before declining to show anyone the slides.

The White House said Trump had completed "the biggest and best part of the project, possibly ever," and that the other two members were "lucky he even showed up to the meeting, which many people are saying he organised."

Meanwhile, the rest of the class — Earth, population 8 billion — has reportedly entered the "please just present and sit down" phase of the assignment.

"We're so tired," said a representative for the international community, who asked not to be named because the project isn't due until Friday. "Every semester it's the same. Three guys, one poster, and somehow the rest of us get marked down for it."

**Breakout sessions scheduled**

Agenda items include a two-hour breakout session in which each leader retreats to a separate room to tell his own delegation that the other two are "impossible to work with," followed by a joint working lunch described in official materials as "the part where everyone pretends the group chat isn't called something horrible."

Analysts note the group has already missed several internal deadlines, including "the part where you divide up the work" and "the icebreaker," and has now entered the classic end-stage phase where all three members simultaneously email the teacher — in this case, the United Nations — to complain about each other.

One analyst said the summit was unlikely to produce a final submission, but would "definitely produce a very long shared document that all three parties edited at 3am and none will agree to present."

A local man in Beijing said he hoped the project would wrap up soon because "the whole street is closed for their presentation and I just want to get noodles."

At press time, all three leaders were reported to be fighting over who gets to hold the poster during the presentation, while the rest of the class quietly asked the teacher whether it was too late to switch groups.
